title: The Kindly Cellar
premise: August Montrose, an urban explorer who documents forgotten spaces as a form of devotion, discovers a tunnel network beneath her hometown that appears on no survey — and at its heart, a cellar where the town's missing have been 'kept' by something ancient that counts its residents like a miser counts coins. When her childhood imaginary friend, Wren, appears on her porch unchanged after twenty years, August realizes the thing in the cellar has been waiting for her to come home, and that her family's names are already on its ledger. To save them, she must understand the count, unmake the bargain her grandmother struck generations ago, and offer the one thing the cellar cannot document: a self freely surrendered. In the end, August takes her grandmother's place not as a prisoner but as the new keeper of the count, rewriting the ledger so the kindly cellar forgets her family — and she becomes the story no survey will ever record.
about_author: Astrid Vane is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing basements, cisterns, and sealed sub-basements of decommissioned public buildings. She writes horror about places that remember people better than people remember themselves.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: August's POV. She maps an unmapped tunnel beneath the old waterworks, documenting obsessively as ritual. The tunnel bends toward her childhood street instead of away from it. Emotional beat: unease dressed up as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her imaginary friend from age seven stands on her mother's porch, unchanged, greeting her by name. Wren says only: 'You're almost late.' Emotional beat: vertigo between nostalgia and dread.

chapters.title: The Family Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV. In her grandmother's attic she finds a handwritten census of the Montrose line, each name annotated with dates — including her own, dated next week. Emotional beat: the past is not finished with her.

chapters.title: Mother Doesn't Remember
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her mother, Delia, dismisses Wren entirely and can't recall her own sister, who vanished in 1989. August finds the aunt's name crossed out in the ledger. Emotional beat: gaslit grief.

chapters.title: Down Where the Count Begins
chapters.summary: August's POV. She returns to the tunnels and reaches the cellar: rows of doors, warm light, and a voice politely asking her to sign in. She flees without signing. Emotional beat: terror wrapped in hospitality.

chapters.title: The Kindly Voice
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV: the cellar itself speaks, explaining it keeps people safe, counted, belonging. It has never lost a resident. Emotional beat: seductive, reasonable evil.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she was never imaginary — she was the previous keeper's emissary, sent to fetch August as a child; August's grandmother refused the trade. Emotional beat: betrayal inside love.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Bargain
chapters.summary: August's POV. A found cassette tape: Grandmother Ida negotiated a deferral — one generation spared if the cellar could keep waiting for August specifically. Emotional beat: inherited debt.

chapters.title: Doors Opening
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Doors around the house begin opening onto the cellar corridor. Delia, memory-frayed, feels strangely welcomed there. Emotional beat: the horror of wanting to belong.

chapters.title: The Missing Census
chapters.summary: August's POV. She cross-references decades of disappearances with the ledger and finds the cellar has been counting the whole town, slowly, for a century. Emotional beat: scale of the threat revealed.

chapters.title: Brother Comes Home
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her estranged brother Theo arrives for Thanksgiving, already half-enchanted — he dreamed the cellar invited him. Emotional beat: family reunion as trap.

chapters.title: Rules of Hospitality
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren teaches August the cellar's rules: it cannot take what refuses to be kept, but refusal must be witnessed and named aloud. Emotional beat: hope with fine print.

chapters.title: First Attempt
chapters.summary: August's POV. August tries to formally refuse for the whole family; the cellar counters by showing each of them their deepest loneliness, answered. Theo wavers. Emotional beat: refusal is harder than fear.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: August's POV. She enters a door deliberately and finds the kept ones — preserved, contented, including her aunt, who begs her to stay. Emotional beat: pity weaponized.

chapters.title: The Count Advances
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The ledger updates itself; Delia's date moves closer. The house grows warmer, more welcoming, harder to leave. Emotional beat: comfort as suffocation.

chapters.title: Ida's Mistake
chapters.summary: August's POV. August learns Ida's deferral failed because Ida tried to trick the count rather than face it; deception gave the cellar its claim. Emotional beat: understanding the true terms.

chapters.title: Unmaking the Signature
chapters.summary: August's POV. With Wren as witness, August attempts to void her entry in the ledger by renouncing what the cellar values most — her documentation, her need to be recorded. Emotional beat: sacrifice rehearsal.

chapters.title: Theo Signs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Broken by the cellar's promise of belonging, Theo signs himself in. August arrives seconds too late. Emotional beat: devastating midpoint-to-climax loss.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax begins: August descends to retrieve Theo before his door closes forever, armed only with the rule of witnessed refusal. Emotional beat: desperate courage.

chapters.title: Freely Surrendered
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax. August offers herself as keeper — not taken but choosing — and rewrites the ledger, striking every Montrose name, trading her documented life for her family's freedom. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia wakes remembering everything, Theo beside her, both free; the tunnels are gone from every map, including August's notebooks. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Epilogue, ambiguous POV. Years later, an urban explorer finds a fresh, unmapped tunnel and a neat hand annotating the walls: directions out, and a warning to hurry home. Emotional beat: August endures, unseen, still keeping count kindly.
